validity.researcher_notes: Sheet Capacity=3400.00 MMcf/d does not match any source found. Enbridge's own factsheet states 'Peak day capacity: 3.6 Bcf/d' (=3,600 MMcf/d) for the whole Westcoast/BC Pipeline system -- and critically this is not a recent change: the Wayback snapshot from 2023-08-17 (the EXACT date this row was last updated) already states the same 3.6 Bcf/d figure verbatim, so 3400 was not correct even as of GEM's own LastUpdated timestamp. Two current (2026) Enbridge press releases found independently of the harvested citation pool (enbridge.com/media-center/news/details?id=123887 and id=123874, both re: the Enbridge-KKR Westcoast joint venture, Aug/Apr 2026) restate the identical 'up to 3.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day' figure and add that capacity is expected to rise further to 3.9 Bcf/d once the Sunrise Expansion Program enters service -- so 3.6 Bcf/d is the stable, current baseline, not a stray or since-superseded number. I could not find a second, non-Enbridge source stating the SAME total-system metric: the CER pipeline profile only publishes point-specific capacity ('At Huntingdon/FortisBC Lower Mainland, the capacity is approximately 1.7 Bcf/d') rather than a system peak-day total, so it is not directly comparable and does not corroborate either 3400 or 3600 -- I checked it precisely because the brief flags CER capacity data as a lead, and it comes up short on this specific figure. Tier is medium (single origin -- Enbridge -- albeit stated identically and consistently across a factsheet at the row's own update date and two independent 2026 press releases). Never found any source supporting the current 3400 figure. This is a material (~6%), material spec disagreement -- flagging as a concern rather than silently adding a ref to the current value.

Second-source search: Enbridge's own Energy Infrastructure Assets factsheet corroborates only indirectly -- it notes the Aitken Creek storage facility, 'located in the heart of the prolific Montney production region,' connects to 'Enbridge's Westcoast (BC) Pipeline,' which ties Montney to Westcoast but doesn't state it as directly as CER does, so I did not count it as a second full-strength source. This row is the whole Westcoast/BC Pipeline SYSTEM (Fort Nelson to Sumas), not one loop -- like the batch's other network rows (CIG, TIGT, Transwestern, Alliance) it has been built and expanded in named loop segments of differing diameter across 70 years (original 1955-57 mainline plus Wyndwood, Spruce Ridge, T-South, Jackfish Lake, Aspen Point, Birch Grove, and now the Sunrise Expansion Program). Two independent secondary histories (Wikipedia's Frank McMahon article and threeminutehistorycanada.substack.com) DO state the ORIGINAL 1955-57 mainline was 'Canada's first big-inch (30-inch) natural gas pipeline' -- but staging '30' as THE Diameter for a row that now represents a much larger, multi-loop, multi-diameter current system would misrepresent it as if the whole system were still 30-inch pipe. Left UNRESOLVED rather than force a partial number; the 30-inch original-mainline detail is recorded here for whoever next builds a proper multi-value figure from the individual expansion-loop CER dockets (several of which were in the row's harvested citation pool but not opened this pass -- see the confirmed-caveat validity note).

A network row of this age and scale plausibly has no single system-wide pressure rating in the public sources I could reach this pass; left UNRESOLVED rather than guess. Not checked: CER REGDOCS facility applications [Folder 90718], which would likely state design pressure per segment but require digging through individual docket filings beyond this pass's scope.

LEAD, not staged: two independent secondary histories (Wikipedia's Frank McMahon article; threeminutehistorycanada.substack.com) both state the original 1955-57 construction cost as 'roughly $170 million' -- but neither states a currency explicitly (Canadian company/project of that era, so CAD is plausible, but the same history also cites a separate '$400-million' 1954 GAS-SALE contract with the U.S.-based Pacific Northwest Pipeline Corp, so a USD figure can't be ruled out either). Per this batch's own caution that half of batch 1's researched SegmentCost values didn't survive primary sources, and given the currency here is genuinely ambiguous rather than just unstated, left UNRESOLVED rather than stage a value with a guessed currency code. Also, this $170M would only cover the original 1955-57 mainline, not the system's many later expansions (Wyndwood $170.3M 2017, Spruce Ridge $564.5M 2018, T-South 2018 $329M, Jackfish Lake $216.3M 2017 -- all named in the row's own harvested CER citations but not opened this pass), so even a confirmed $170M would only be a partial SegmentCost for a row that represents the whole system.
